text.p: Precious metal prices began the week above Friday's closing levels and it was silver which attracted most of the light interest in the afternoon, dealers said.
"What a difference a week makes," said one dealer, referring to the anxiety in the market during last week's descent to a 40-month low gold fixing of $348.00 per ounce.
Gold was fixed at $353.60 on Monday afternoon, up from $353.10 at the morning fix and $352.50 on Friday afternoon.
The Comex February contract was $1.40 ahead at $354.80 just after the fixing at 1500 GMT.

"Gold may have to play catch up with silver which is looking a bit toppish on the charts but can probable still manage 10-15 cents on the upside before coming back eight or nine (Cents)," one dealer said.
However technical analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge was rather less sanguine.
"I would warn against any premature optimism as there is a wide belt of resistance between 500 and 510 and even more between 520 and 540 cents," she said.
Several dealers reckoned $5.00 was the short term target for silver but that was also the most focal strike price in this week's OTC option expiry.
"It should stay steady at least until the option expiry," one dealer said.
For gold however the expiry was less critical as the market's fall since the beginning of the year had taken the price into an area where it was deeply away for the money, dealers said.
Although gold was seen still in an overall downtrend, its pick-up from last week's low had encouraged buying on dips with $352.50 seen as a short term support, dealers said.
Platinum and palladium also reflected the firmer tone, albeit very quietly.
Platinum was marked up $2.20 to $359.45/$360.45 and palladium was 50 cents firmer at $122.50/$123.50 having moved in a very narrow range all day.
